idiom_name: traits as components: mixin composition, with self-types for the Cake pattern
implementation_notes: The Scala Tour documents traits as the composition unit ('class composition with mixins') and self-types as the way for a trait to require another without extending it, and the Cake pattern turns that into the Scala reading of this pattern: each domain becomes a ...Component trait exposing an abstract member, dependent traits declare self-types, and a Registry object mixes everything together, resolving the wiring at compile time. Prefer plain mixins (a class extends the traits whose behaviour it has) when capabilities are fixed, and reserve self-typed component traits for large hierarchies - the boilerplate is a real cost. Mixins are static, so runtime swapping means a var or a List of trait-typed components instead.
pitfalls: Self-typed component traits initialise badly: a val in one component used during another component's initialisation is still null or zero, producing NPEs or silently zero values - the classic Cake-pattern failure.
Trait mixin composition is fixed at compile time, so runtime component changes require a var or List of trait-typed components rather than mixins.
The Cake pattern needs boilerplate that Baeldung judges 'probably not worth it for small class hierarchies'; do not use self-typed component traits where constructor injection would do.
